subtitle: When the Kaveri Met the Kaveri of the West

panels.shot: split-diagonal composition showing two kings facing opposite directions, one in Chola armour by the Kaveri delta, the other in Ganga attire by the sandbanks of Talakad
panels.action: Rajaraja Chola I stands stern and commanding beside a broad Kaveri canal, while Rakkasa Ganga stands thoughtful on the sandy banks of Talakad, a hazy battlefield between them under a looming monsoon sky.

dialogue.text: In c.1004, Rajaraja Chola’s banners reached Talakad—and with one campaign, the old Ganga kingdom of Gangapadi slipped into a new imperial order.

i18n.hi: लगभग १००४ में, राजराजा चोल के ध्वज तालाकाड तक पहुँचे—एक ही मुहिम में पुराना गंगा राज्य गंगापाडि नए साम्राज्य में समा गया।

panels.shot: wide aerial over the Kaveri delta, then fading into the uplands of Gangapadi
panels.action: A sweeping vista shows the lush, irrigated Kaveri delta fading into a drier, undulating plateau with scattered tanks and fields, hinting at the long distance between Chola country and Gangapadi.

dialogue.text: From the rich Kaveri delta to the dry plains of Gangapadi lay not just forests and hills, but rival tax systems, temples, and chiefs. Rajaraja Chola wanted them all stitched into one empire.

i18n.hi: समृद्ध कावेरी डेल्टा से सूखे गंगापाडि तक सिर्फ जंगल-पहाड़ नहीं, अलग कर-व्यवस्थाएँ, मंदिर और सरदार थे। राजराजा चोल सबको एक ही साम्राज्य में पिरोना चाहता था।

panels.shot: close, oblique shot of a stone inscription being chiseled, lit by lamplight
panels.action: A sculptor’s hand chisels crisp Grantha and Tamil letters onto a stone slab, with faint words like 'Gangapadi' and 'Nolambapadi' halfway carved, oil lamps casting sharp shadows on the temple wall.

dialogue.text: His meikeerthis proclaim it proudly: Rajaraja, conqueror of Gangapadi, Nolambapadi and Tadigaipadi. Yet these are victor’s lines, carved after the dust settled.

i18n.hi: उसकी मेखेर्ति खुलकर बोलीं: गंगापाडि, नोलंबापाडि और तडिगैपाडि का विजेता राजराजा। पर ये विजेता की पंक्तियाँ हैं, धूल बैठने के बाद उकेरी गईं।

panels.shot: medium two-shot, but with the kings in different architectural frames to show distance and contrast
panels.action: On one side, Rajaraja Chola I stands in a hall of the Kaveri delta, backed by orderly pillars and palm-leaf records; on the other, Rakkasa Ganga is in a modest court with Jaina basadis in the background, scrolls and spears at his side.

dialogue.text: Facing him in the west was Rakkasa Ganga, last strong Ganga king, ruling from regions around Talakad and Shravanabelagola, his autonomy already squeezed by neighbours and overlords.

i18n.hi: पश्चिम में उसके सामने था रक्कस गंगा, आखिरी ताकतवर गंगा राजा, तालाकाड और श्रवणबेलगोला के इर्द-गिर्द से राज करता, पड़ोसियों और अधिपतियों ने जिसकी आजादी पहले ही दबा दी थी।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Rakkasa Ganga with map-like floor painting at his feet
panels.action: Rakkasa Ganga stands over a painted board showing Gangapadi, Nolambapadi and surrounding regions, small tokens marking neighbouring powers pressing in from all sides, his face lined with concern.

dialogue.text: Late Ganga inscriptions show a shrinking world—old grants curtailed, overlord names changing. Gangapadi was still theirs in name, but power was shared, bargained, and sometimes taken.

i18n.hi: देर के गंगा शिलालेख एक सिकुड़ती दुनिया दिखाते हैं—पुरानी दान-ज़मीनें कटीं, अधिपतियों के नाम बदलते गए। गंगापाडि नाम से उनका ही था, पर ताकत बाँटी, मोल-तोल की और कई बार छीनी गई।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Rajaraja in war council with generals around a map
panels.action: Rajaraja Chola I leans over a palm-leaf map spread on a low table, commanders in mail and cloth ringed around him, his finger tracing routes toward Gangapadi’s fertile tracts and river crossings.

dialogue.text: For Rajaraja, Gangapadi meant more than glory. It meant control of upland grain, cattle, and trade routes—fresh revenue to feed temples, armies, and irrigation in the Chola heartland.

i18n.hi: राजराजा के लिए गंगापाडि सिर्फ शान नहीं था। ऊपरी इलाकों का अनाज, मवेशी और व्यापारी रास्तों पर काबू था—नया धन, जो चोल धरती के मंदिरों, फौजों और सिंचाई को खिलाए।

panels.shot: wide shot of a marching Chola column entering a forested pass
panels.action: A disciplined Chola army column with elephants, cavalry, and infantry advances through a forested pass, banners showing the Chola tiger snapping in the wind, scouts moving ahead along the ridgeline.

dialogue.text: Sometime around 1004, his forces moved west. The meikeerthi condenses months of marches and skirmishes into a single boast: that Gangapadi had been brought under the Chola umbrella.

i18n.hi: करीब १००४ के आस-पास उसकी फौजें पश्चिम चलीं। मेखेर्ति महीनों की चढ़ाइयों और मुठभेड़ों को एक घमंड में समेट देती है: कि गंगापाडि अब चोलों की छाँव में आ गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Rakkasa Ganga looking out over Talakad’s sandbanks and the Kaveri
panels.action: Rakkasa Ganga stands on the sandy rise of Talakad, the Kaveri curling below and small shrines and houses dotted along the bank, soldiers and local chiefs gathered behind him awaiting orders.

dialogue.speaker: rajaraja_chola_i_and_rakkasa_ganga
dialogue.text: “Talakad has seen many banners. Will it remember ours?”

i18n.hi: "तालाकाड ने बहुत से झंडे देखे हैं। क्या वो हमारा याद रखेगा?"

panels.shot: long shot of opposing forces facing off near Talakad, viewed from a raised sandbank
panels.action: Across the river plain near Talakad, two forces stand arrayed: Chola lines tight and deep, Ganga troops and allied contingents looser but proud, the Kaveri glinting between them under heavy clouds.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions do not narrate every blow. They simply attest that the Ganga heartland—Talakad, Gangapadi—fell into Chola hands, and Rakkasa Ganga’s sovereignty was broken.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख हर वार की कथा नहीं कहते। बस ये जताते हैं कि गंगा का दिल—तालाकाड, गंगापाडि—चोलों के हाथ आया, और रक्कस गंगा की सत्ता टूट गई।

panels.shot: dramatic medium close-up of Rajaraja receiving word of success from a dust-covered messenger
panels.action: In a Chola camp pavilion, Rajaraja Chola I sits composed as a dust-stained courier kneels, presenting a palm-leaf; outside, silhouettes of elephants and banners hint at victory celebrations beginning.

dialogue.text: Rajaraja’s meikeerthi from Tanjavur reports the outcome with calm confidence: the three ‘padi’s of the west were now tied to his throne, their revenues pledged to his great projects.

i18n.hi: तंजावुर की राजराजा की मेखेर्ति नतीजा सहज भरोसे से लिखती है: पश्चिम के तीन ‘पाडि’ अब उसके सिंहासन से बँधे हैं, उनकी आमदनी उसके महा-प्रकल्पों को समर्पित है।

panels.shot: somber medium shot of Rakkasa Ganga in a dim hall, crown set aside
panels.action: Rakkasa Ganga sits alone in a darkened hall, his crown resting beside him on a low platform, a single lamp burning as outside faint sounds of departing soldiers drift in.

dialogue.text: For Rakkasa Ganga, the records grow faint after this moment. Ganga kings appear now as lesser lords, their titles and donations acknowledging powerful overlords instead of claiming equal rank.

i18n.hi: रक्कस गंगा के लिए, इस पल के बाद अभिलेख धुंधले पड़ते हैं। गंगा राजा अब छोटे सरदार बनकर दिखते हैं, उनके खिताब और दान बराबरी नहीं, ताकतवर अधिपतियों को मान्यता देते हैं।

panels.shot: wide interior of a shrine at Shravanabelagola with donors of different eras portrayed together
panels.action: Inside a basadi at Shravanabelagola, old Ganga-era donor figures carved on stone share the wall with newer inscriptions that mention Chola and later overlords, a Jain monk seated quietly in the foreground.

dialogue.text: Yet at Shravanabelagola and other centres, Ganga names endure on stone. Under Chola and then Hoysala power, local chiefs and Jaina patrons kept their lineages alive through gifts and memory.

i18n.hi: फिर भी श्रवणबेलगोला और दूसरे केन्द्रों में गंगा नाम पत्थरों पर टिका रहा। चोल और फिर होयसल ताकत के नीचे, स्थानीय सरदारों और जैन दानियों ने अपनी वंश-लकीरें दान और यादों से बचाए रखीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Chola official measuring a field in Gangapadi with village elders watching
panels.action: A Chola revenue officer in simple yet distinct attire stretches a rope across a field in Gangapadi, marking it with pegs, while village elders and a former Ganga retainer look on, some wary, some resigned.

dialogue.text: Burton Stein sees this as a change in control more than a simple conquest: Chola officers, records, and taxes overlaying old village structures, binding Gangapadi into a wider agrarian state.

i18n.hi: बर्टन स्टाइन इसे साधारण फतह से ज्यादा हक बदलने की कहानी मानते हैं: चोल अफसर, रजिस्टर और कर पुरानी गाँव-व्यवस्था पर चढ़ गए, गंगापाडि को बड़े कृषक राज्य में बाँधते हुए।

panels.shot: wide temple courtyard in the Chola country with an inscription listing Gangapadi among endowments
panels.action: In a Chola temple courtyard, priests and laymen move about as a large inscription slab lists lands endowed from Gangapadi, Nolambapadi and Tadigaipadi, Rajaraja’s name framed above the place names.

dialogue.text: In the east, Rajaraja’s temple slabs quietly record the shift. Lands in Gangapadi now fund lamps, food-offerings, and festivals in distant Kaveri temples, tying upland harvests to delta rituals.

i18n.hi: पूरब में, राजराजा के मंदिरों की स्लैब चुपचाप ये बदलाव लिखती हैं। गंगापाडि की ज़मीनें अब दूर कावेरी के मंदिरों की दीपक, भोजन-भोग और उत्सवों को चलाती हैं, पहाड़ी फसलों को डेल्टा की पूजा से जोड़ती हैं।

panels.shot: split-panel style long shot, one half showing later Hoysala structures around Shravanabelagola, the other half a faded memory of Ganga banners
panels.action: One side shows a later Hoysala-style shrine near Shravanabelagola with ornate pillars; the other shows faint, ghost-like Ganga banners over the same landscape, fading into the sky as new emblems rise.

dialogue.text: Later, Hoysala kings would rise in these same lands. The Ganga realm, once sovereign, lived on as a layer beneath newer powers, its symbols recalled in place-names, genealogies, and stone.

i18n.hi: बाद में, इन्हीं इलाकों से होयसल राजा उठेंगे। कभी खुदमुख्तार गंगा राज्य नई ताकतों के नीचे एक परत बनकर जीवित रहा, उसके चिन्ह जगह-नामों, वंशावलियों और पत्थर में गूँजते रहे।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of Talakad’s sands and the Kaveri with faint silhouettes of both kings in the sky
panels.action: The sands of Talakad stretch under a soft evening light, small shrines peeking from the dunes by the Kaveri; in the faint clouds above, the silhouettes of Rajaraja and Rakkasa Ganga seem to look down in silence.

dialogue.text: Rajaraja’s victory ended Ganga sovereignty, but not Ganga memory. At Talakad and Shravanabelagola, we still see how kingdoms fall, yet their people, shrines, and stories learn to live under new power.

i18n.hi: राजराजा की जीत ने गंगा की सत्ता खत्म की, गंगा की याद नहीं। तालाकाड और श्रवणबेलगोला में आज भी दिखता है कैसे राज्य गिरते हैं, पर लोग, देवालय और कहानियाँ नई ताकत के नीचे जीना सीख लेते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Kaveri Met the Kaveri of the West
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब कावेरी ने पश्चिम की कावेरी से मुलाकात की
